metadata.name: Ecodesign for React (and Preact)
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for React and Preact: avoided re-renders, split routes, virtualised lists, cleaned-up effects.

rendu.name: React — rendering
rendu.description: A re-render that changes nothing still costs a diff on every visitor's device (RGESN Frontend).

rules.title: Effect without a dependency array
rules.description: useEffect with no dependency array runs after every render. When it fetches, the component re-renders, which runs the effect again: the loop is invisible in the code and obvious in the network tab.
rules.recommendation: Give every effect its dependency array, and return a cleanup that aborts the request or clears the timer.

example.good: useEffect(() => { const c = new AbortController(); fetchData(c.signal); return () => c.abort() }, [id])

rules.note: An effect written across several lines is not seen by a line-based pattern; this catches the single-line form, which is the common one.

rules.title: Long list rendered in full
rules.description: Rendering ten thousand rows creates ten thousand DOM nodes for the twenty the user can see. The device pays in memory, in layout and in every subsequent interaction.
rules.recommendation: Virtualise the list, or paginate it. Give the items stable keys so React can reuse nodes instead of rebuilding them.
rules.source_note: Adapted from the Green Codex rule LANG-REACT-002 (Institut du Numerique Responsable), whose rule content is published under CC BY 4.0. Reworded for this format; the patterns are specific to this audit.
rules.note: This rule shares an extension with another framework's rule set, so it also stays silent in a file that imports the other framework: the pattern alone cannot tell which one is in play.

rules.title: New object or function passed as a prop
rules.description: An inline object or arrow function is a new reference on every render, so every memoised child below re-renders anyway. The memoisation is paid for and does nothing.
rules.recommendation: Hoist the value out of the component, or wrap it in useMemo or useCallback when profiling shows the child actually re-renders.
